description: Linear equation with the variable on both sides, integer coefficients: {a}x + b = {c}x + d, solved by transposition. Matches the shape already authored by hand as le-q01 through le-q05.
hardConstraints: a !== c (otherwise the x term cancels entirely after transposition — division by zero)

a and c are both authored as positive in this version — negative leading coefficients (e.g. le-q05's '14 - x') are a real variant of this family but are out of scope for this first template; noted as future work
hintTemplate: Move all the x terms to one side of the equation and all the constant terms to the other side.
Combine like terms, then divide both sides by the coefficient of x to isolate it.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Forgetting to flip the sign of a term when it is transposed across the equals sign.
misconception.why: Treating transposition as copying a term to the other side rather than as a sign-flipping move — the shorthand for subtracting/adding that term on both sides.
misconception.remediationHint: When a term crosses the equals sign, its sign flips: a term that was positive becomes negative, and vice versa.
